hints.title: Pigeonhole Density Observation
hints.text: The repeated number appears n times in an array of size 2n. It must appear at distance 1, 2, or 3 from another identical copy.

hints.title: Local Window Comparison
hints.text: Compare elements within distance up to 3. If any match is found, that element is guaranteed to be the n-repeated value.

hints.title: Direct Scan or Set Lookup
hints.text: Iterate index i from 0 to len(nums) - 1. If nums[i] equals nums[i - 1], nums[i - 2], or nums[i - 3], return nums[i]. Alternatively maintain a seen collection and return the first duplicate encountered.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: half the length of nums
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full frequency sorting takes O(N log N) time, which is unnecessarily slow for identifying a majority duplicate.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Inspecting small window offsets of size 1, 2, and 3 takes strictly O(1) extra space and O(N) operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain via the pigeonhole principle why identical copies cannot be separated by more than 2 elements everywhere.
complexity.notes: Worst case gap of 3 occurs in permutations like [1, 2, 3, 1].
